en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Four Heavenly Kings, translated by the Śramaṇa Zhìyán of Liangzhou together with Bǎoyún during the Song Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park. The Buddha...
He addressed his disciples:
"Be cautious of your thoughts; do not crave the six desires.
Rinse away the passions to remove defilement; do not seek to be foremost."
Internally, one should maintain purity; externally, one should practice filial piety.
With the four immeasurable minds, one should serve and nourish those who gave birth to one.

Entering the honored temple at dawn, one should prostrate and repent of transgressions; receiving instructions in the morning and reciting in the evening, one should contemplate the wondrous meaning of the sutras.
One uses the Buddha’s weighty precepts to treat the disease of mental defilement;
observing the fasts in a pure and quiet place, one practices breath-counting and meditative concentration;
reversing the flow and exhausting the source, one seeks the truth of the Way.
Life is like a flash of lightning; it vanishes in an instant.
On days of fasting, one must scrutinize the mind, guard the body, and restrain the speech; for on these days of fasting, the devas observe the good and evil of human beings.

Mount Sumeru is the site of the second heaven, the Trāyastriṃśa (Heaven of the Thirty-three). Its Lord of Devas is named Indra; his merit and virtue are most majestic, and he presides over the four heavens.

The four celestial kings of these heavens are the Kings of the Four Quarters, each governing one direction. On the eighth day of every month, they dispatch their messengers to descend and inspect the world, observing the mental thoughts, verbal speech, and physical actions—whether good or evil—of emperors, ministers, and subjects, as well as the classes of dragons, ghosts, insects, flying creatures, crawling beings, and all that wriggles and moves.
On the fourteenth day, they dispatch their crown princes to descend.
On the fifteenth day, the Four Heavenly Kings descend;
on the twenty-third day, their messengers descend again;
and on the twenty-ninth day, the Prince descends once more.
On the thirtieth day, the Four Kings descended once more.
When the Four Kings descend, the sun, the moon, the five planets, and the twenty-eight lunar mansions, along with all the devas therein, descend together in unison.
The Four Kings commanded them, saying:
"Vigilantly observe sentient beings and administer their fortune or misfortune.
If, on this day, they take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha of Bhikṣus;
Purifying the mind and observing the fasts, practicing charity toward the poor and destitute;
upholding the precepts, practicing patience, exerting diligence, and cultivating meditative concentration;
studying and expounding the sutras to enlighten and transform those who are blind and ignorant.
Filial and obedient toward one's two parents, serving the Triple Gem;
prostrating to receive the Dharma and practicing the four immeasurable minds to compassionately nurture all sentient beings—one who possesses such distinctions shall be instructed by Śakra Devendra.
"If one cultivates virtue extensively and practices diligence without slackening, Śakra and his thirty-three ministers will all rejoice together.
Śakra shall command the messengers of death to increase their lifespan and extend their years;
he shall dispatch various benevolent deities to protect and guard their persons."
According to the number of precepts observed, if one upholds a single precept, five deities shall protect it;

if one possesses all five precepts, twenty-five deities shall guard the gates and doors, causing calamities, epidemics, various malevolent influences, and secret plots to be extinguished, ensuring that there are no evil dreams at night,
and that officials, thieves, water, fire, and disasters shall ultimately fail to cause harm.

To avert calamities and extinguish怪异 (strange phenomena), these four immeasurables, the five precepts, and the six fasts are like a great body of water that extinguishes a small fire; how could there be anything that is not extinguished?
When their life comes to an end, they shall welcome their spirits to be reborn in celestial palaces made of the seven treasures in the heavens; there is no wish that shall not be fulfilled.

However, if there are those who do not save the lives of sentient beings, who are defiled and impure, thieves, who commit adultery with the wives of others, who engage in double-tongued speech, harsh abuse, lying, and frivolous talk, who practice malevolent incantations and curses, who are jealous, hateful, and deluded, who act contrary to the Way and are unfilial, who violate the Buddha and the Dharma, who slander the *bhikṣu* Sangha, or who invert the discourse on good and evil—if such practitioners exist, the Four Heavenly Kings will report this. Śakra and all the devas will collectively be displeased; the benevolent deities will no longer protect them, and they will immediately cause the sun and moon to lose their radiance, the stars to lose their courses, and wind and rain to fall out of season.
"Those in the present world who desire to reform their past and cultivate their future must purify their minds and observe solemn austerity;
they should confess their transgressions before the Three Honored Ones, practice the four immeasurable states to nourish their parents,
remain loyal to the sovereign, and offer remonstrance with a compassionate heart."
Exerting sincerity without deception, one returns to the cultivation of former sages;
casting off impure conduct, one follows the path of purity.
"If there are those who reform their deviant practices to follow what is upright and true, Śakra and the Four Heavenly Kings will all rejoice."
The sun and moon were clear and bright, and the constellations followed their regular courses;
wind and rain accorded with the seasons, and noxious vapors dissipated;
heaven sent down sweet dew, and the earth brought forth springs of moisture.
By consuming the flavorful essence of water and grain, one suffers little illness;
one's complexion becomes radiant and lustrous, and one’s lifespan is further extended.
In life, one shall not enter prison; at death, one shall attain rebirth in the heavens.
By virtue of their merit and aspirations, they naturally fly through the air;
they possess mastery over life and death, with a radiance like sunlight upon their necks;
their food is digested spontaneously, free from the affliction of excrement or urine.
The body is fragrant and pure, and the breath is sweetly scented.
Today, the sun, moon, and stars are the palaces and abodes of the various devas!
Their halls of seven treasures hang suspended in the void, according to their mental aspirations.

At the end of their life, they will descend to be born into the families of marquises and kings; their countenances will be radiant and glorious, bringing joy to the hearts of all who see them. Encountering the Buddha and meeting the Dharma and the sages, they will practice with continuous diligence, never associating with evil, and shall surely attain Nirvana.
All of this is brought about by the five precepts and ten wholesome paths, by restraining the emotions and desires, and by observing the six fast days!

During the time of Krakucchanda Buddha, the human lifespan was sixty thousand years; the people were naturally inclined toward non-action, protecting others as they would themselves, with impartiality and no duality.
After that Buddha passed into extinction, the true teaching declined and grew thin;
the people lacked correct conduct and gradually turned toward evil.
Their lifespan decreased day by day until it reached one hundred years.
After my passing as a Sugata, the people will violate the Buddha’s teachings and there will no longer be filial sons;
the Lord of Death will shorten their reckonings, and their lifespans will diminish day by day.
The celestial deities will offer no protection, and calamitous epidemics and malevolent spirits will daily come to inflict harm.
Calamities and portents follow one after another; my wishes are thwarted, and misfortunes run rampant.
In life, I am cast into the prison of the king’s law; in death, I shall enter the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals.
If one emerges from this state to become human, one will surely be of low station.
Good and evil follow the person like the five grains; according to what is sown, one reaps its fruit.
It is also like writing at night: when the fire is extinguished, the characters remain.
When the body dies, the name perishes, yet misfortune and fortune remain imperishable.
Be careful to guard your mind, restrain your body, and maintain your speech; through the five precepts and the ten wholesome actions, you may attain the Way.
"I have now attained Buddhahood because of the accumulation of my practices!
Upon hearing this sutra, all the bhikṣus were filled with great joy; they prostrated themselves before the Buddha and departed.
This was the *Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Four Heavenly Kings*.
